title: GPU CI: Artifact Sharding, Hermetic Builds, and Benchmarking Pipeline
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood's recommended pattern for large-scale GPU CI that supports: incremental artifact sharding, hermetic builds for reproducibility, integrated micro-benchmarks during CI, and safe promotion of build artifacts into the golden-image and release pipelines. The guidance is intended for infra engineers, platform teams, and any repo that builds GPU-optimized artifacts (containers, wheels, compiled kernels).

Goals and constraints:
- Fast developer feedback loop (< 20 minutes for warm CI runs) while preserving reproducible artifacts for production.
- Deterministic artifact identification (content-addressable) and shardable upload to artifact storage (S3/GCS).
- Low network and egress cost through aggressive caching and shard reuse.
- Integrated perf smoke-tests and regression gates that block promotion on significant slowdowns.

Key concepts:
1) Artifact sharding: split large build outputs (e.g., 10–50GB compiled kernels or dataset slices) into deterministic shards keyed by (repo, commit, build-target, toolchain, shard-index). Shards are uploaded independently so retryable failures affect only a shard.
2) Hermetic builds: builds must declare inputs (pip/conda lockfiles, Bazel/Make labels, compiler versions) and produce a content-addressable manifest (build.manifest.json) listing artifact checksums and provenance.
3) In-pipeline benchmarks: lightweight microbenchmarks run on a cached GPU runner; results are stored alongside artifacts and compared to baseline using a simple delta threshold.
4) Promotion flow: artifacts are signed and promoted to a release bucket only after unit/perf tests and an attestation step.

Pipeline stages (recommended ordering):
- prepare-checkout (owner: repo team): fetch submodules, lockfiles; compute build key hash.
- compile-and-shard (owner: build infra): build with deterministic flags; split outputs into shards (size target 256–1024MB).
- shard-upload (owner: build infra): parallel upload shards with retry/backoff; record shard manifest.
- integrity-and-sign (owner: security infra): verify checksums and apply artifact signing (Sigstore or internal KMS).
- perf-smoke (owner: perf infra): run 5 representative microbenchmarks on a warmed GPU node; record latency/tokens/samples.
- acceptance-tests (owner: repo team): functional tests against containerized artifacts.
- promote-or-rollback (owner: release infra): promote to golden bucket or mark rollback with reason.

Operational details and thresholds:
- Shard TTL: ephemeral shards in the staging bucket expire after 14 days; promoted artifacts kept per retention policy (90 days default, archive to cold storage after 1 year).
- Upload parallelism: default 8 concurrent uploads per runner; backoff policy: exponential, max 5 retries.
- Perf regression gate: block promotion if median latency increase > 5% or > 2 sigma compared to baseline. Alert and require manual review.
- Warm GPU runner SLO: average queue wait < 3 minutes for nightly and < 10 minutes for PR-level perf runs.

Example build manifest (JSON, stored as build.manifest.json):
| Field | Description |
| repo | repository name and URL |
| commit | git SHA |
| toolchain | docker image or compiler version |
| shards | list of shard objects (index, path, sha256) |
| benchmarks | list of perf results with keys and timestamps |

CLI snippets and examples:
- Compute build key (bash):
  BUILD_KEY=$(echo -n "${REPO}:${COMMIT}:${TOOLCHAIN}" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}')
- Upload shard with aws cli:
  aws s3 cp shard-0001.tar.gz s3://redwood-staging/artifacts/${BUILD_KEY}/ --storage-class STANDARD --acl bucket-owner-full-control --expected-sha256 "$(sha256sum shard-0001.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}')"

GitHub Actions / Buildkite example (YAML snippet):
- name: Compile and shard
  runs-on: gpu-runner
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - run: |
        ./scripts/compile.sh --out-dir=artifacts/tmp
        python3 tools/shard_artifacts.py artifacts/tmp --size-mb 512 --out artifacts/shards
    - run: |
        parallel-upload --concurrency 8 artifacts/shards s3://redwood-staging/${{ env.BUILD_KEY }}

shard_artifacts.py (excerpt):
- Splits files by byte size and writes a manifest with sha256 checksums. The script must be deterministic (sorted input list) and avoid timestamped entries in shards.

Hermetic build requirements checklist:
1. All third-party packages pinned to exact versions (requirements.txt / Poetry lock).
2. Build container image specified by SHA (not mutable tags).
3. Compiler flags and ENV are recorded in build.manifest.json.
4. No network access during final packaging stage (optional offline stage to catch implicit network deps).

Benchmarking approach:
- Benchmarks should be small (< 30s) and representative: token generation 256-step latency, throughput for batch sizes 1/8/64, KV cache warm vs cold.
- Results are stored with metadata: runner-id, CUDA/cuDNN versions, GPU instance type, driver, GPU utilization.
- Baselines: nightly promoted artifacts become baselines for next 24 hours. Continuous regression detection triggers triage.

Failure modes and runbook steps (high level):
- shard-upload failures: check runner network, verify S3 credentials permission to staging prefix, retry using documented backoff, optionally re-run compile-and-shard.
- checksum mismatch on integrity: quarantine the artifact, notify security infra, revoke any partial promotions, and kick off a rebuild with the exact build key.
- perf-smoke regression: annotate run with diff to baseline, auto-open a perf-triage ticket under infra-serving runtime; temporarily block promotion if severity high.

Security and signing:
- Use Sigstore/fulcio for ephemeral CI signing where possible; for restricted builds use KMS-authorized signing keys.
- All promoted artifacts must have a signed attestation linking commit -> build.manifest -> benchmark snapshot.

Terraform and IaC integration notes:
- Provide a single Terraform module (infra-ci-artifacts) that creates: staging and release buckets, IAM roles for upload and promotion, lifecycle rules, and SNS topics for promotion events.
- Avoid embedding credentials in pipeline YAML; use short-lived STS creds exchanged via workload identity (GCP) or OIDC (AWS) where possible.

Cost optimization tips:
- Prefer shard dedup by content hash before upload (skip upload if exact hash exists).
- Set lifecycle rules to move artifacts older than 90 days to Infrequent/Cold storage to reduce S3/GCS costs.
- Use burstable spot-backed GPU runners for non-blocking PRs; reserve on-demand for perf and promotion jobs.

Metrics to track (dashboards):
- median compile time per target; 95th percentile shard upload latency; failed shard ratio; perf-smoke pass rate; promotion rate; artifact storage cost by repo.

Rollout plan for repo owners:
1. Opt-in by adding the build.ksh script and shard_artifacts.py and enabling the GPU-runner label on CI.
2. Run in dry-run mode for 2 weeks (uploads to staging but no promotions).
3. Enable perf-smoke gate and tune thresholds for false positives.
4. Flip promotion toggle and retire legacy pipeline.

References and related pages:
- See the golden image pipeline page for promotion semantics and image signing.
- Refer to Terraform module documentation for infra-ci-artifacts for policy and IAM contracts.

Appendix: example artifact manifest (short)
{
  "repo": "github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime",
  "commit": "a1b2c3d4",
  "toolchain": "registry.redwood/ci-compiler@sha256:abcdef",
  "shards": [
    {"index": "000", "path": "shards/000.tar.gz", "sha256": "..."}
  ],
  "benchmarks": [ {"name": "latency-256", "median_ms": 13.2, "runner": "gpu-1"} ]
}
